milestone: Collection — Theme-Scoped, Deduplicated Asset Registry (Phase 5: Creator-Facing Availability Metadata)
slice: Implements Phase 5 of the approved Collection plan -- the one part of Collection that touches the currently-locked .vtheme contract, so it ships with a docs/VTHEME_PACKAGE_SPEC.md update, not treated as 'just more code.' A Collection entry the Theme Author flagged availableToCreator:true must reach the compiled package regardless of whether any Layer currently references it -- that's the whole point of the flag ('collection can have assets which are used in scenes and others which builder would want creator to have access for customization,' the user's own words) -- and Phase 4's own dedup path only ever embedded a Collection entry as a side effect of some Layer's own layer.image pointing at it. packageTheme() (tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js) now walks package_.collectionAssets (already collected there, carrying every entry's internal .ref) right after convergeScenes() runs, and for every entry with availableToCreator===true, guarantees its bytes are embedded at its own stable collection/<id>.png key -- a no-op via memoization if a Scene Layer already embedded it first -- then builds a SEPARATE, sanitized array, package_.creatorCollectionAssets, holding only id/name/kind/relPath/availableToCreator per entry: never the internal .ref, a Builder-session-internal detail that must never leak into a published Theme. The hydrate-and-embed logic itself was extracted out of externalizeSceneImage's own Phase-4 dedup branch into one new shared method, _embedCollectionEntry(entry, package_), reused by both call sites (externalizeSceneImage for the 'a Layer points at this entry' case, packageTheme's new sweep for the 'flagged for reuse but used by nothing at all' case) rather than duplicated -- externalizeSceneImage's own Phase 4 dedup behaviour is byte-identical, confirmed via the unchanged 17/17 Phase 4 suite. buildTheme() gained the exact same 'only when non-empty' pattern already used for frameVariations/representations: theme.collectionAssets = packageData.creatorCollectionAssets only when that array actually has entries, so a Theme with zero availableToCreator entries -- every Theme authored before this phase, or one whose Collection assets are all used only inside Scenes and never flagged for reuse -- compiles with the key simply absent, never an empty array. docs/VTHEME_PACKAGE_SPEC.md gained a full theme.collectionAssets section (both the Story Theme and Artwork Theme JSON examples, plus a dedicated field-by-field writeup covering the sanitized shape, the relPath-resolves-via-ThemeRegistry.resolveAssetRef convention every other image-bearing field already uses, and the one deliberate exception this field represents -- an availableToCreator entry is embedded regardless of Scene usage, unlike every other asset field in the document). Verified via a new, comprehensive Playwright suite (collection_phase5_verify.js, 30/30 assertions, zero console/page errors) driving the REAL, unmodified compile pipeline end to end against a real Blank World Project with a real Scene carrying four distinct cases in one Theme: Entry A (availableToCreator:true, used by a real Layer) is embedded once and listed once in theme.collectionAssets; Entry B (availableToCreator:true, registered standalone via ProjectModel.registerCollectionAsset with zero Layer or Experience referencing it at all) still gets its bytes embedded and still appears in theme.collectionAssets -- the literal proof of the flag's own purpose; Entry C (used by a real Layer, left at its default availableToCreator:false) is still embedded via Phase 4's own unaffected dedup but correctly does NOT appear in theme.collectionAssets, confirming the two concepts are genuinely orthogonal; a fourth, legacy-shaped Decoration Layer (authored directly, never through an Experience, never registered in Collection at all) still converges via exactly today's own per-Layer relPath; every theme.collectionAssets record was confirmed to carry ONLY the sanitized id/name/kind/relPath/availableToCreator fields with the internal .ref field genuinely absent; two consecutive Builds produced a byte-identical theme.collectionAssets array and assets map (determinism, matching this codebase's own already-established Publish guarantee); and a brand-new second World with zero Collection entries at all compiled successfully with theme.collectionAssets confirmed simply absent (undefined), never an empty array. Full regression: both goldenBuild.js suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each) pass unchanged; the Phase 1 (27/27), Phase 2 (28/28), Phase 3 (25/25), and Phase 4 (17/17) suites all pass completely unchanged, confirming zero regression from this phase's own additions. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; tools/world-builder/ (v1) and root Studio are completely untouched -- confined entirely to tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js and docs/VTHEME_PACKAGE_SPEC.md. Phase 6 (a Creator-side 'From This World' browsing row in js/contextPanel.js's Add Something accordion, resolving theme.collectionAssets via the existing, uniform ThemeRegistry.resolveAssetRef -- 'add new' only per the user's own answered 'Both') remains a named, not-yet-started increment -- see /root/.claude/plans/witty-floating-thimble.md for the complete phased rollout.
